stem.text: The height of a weather balloon above the ground, measured in meters, is modeled by a twice-differentiable function A of time t, measured in seconds. It is known that \( A''(4) = -0.5 \). Using correct units, interpret the meaning of \( A''(4) = -0.5 \) in the context of the problem.

answer_key.label: At time t = 4 seconds, the rate at which the height of the balloon is changing is decreasing at a rate of 0.5 meters per second per second.

worked_solution.text: \( A''(4) \) is the rate of change of \( A' \), the rate at which the height of the balloon changes, so it is measured in meters per second per second.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative as the rate of change of a rate

worked_solution.text: The value is negative, so at t = 4 the rate of change of the height of the balloon is itself decreasing, by 0.5 meters per second for each second.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the second derivative gives the direction of change of the rate

options.label: At time t = 4 seconds, the rate at which the height of the balloon is changing is decreasing at a rate of 0.5 meters per second per second.
